toc.title: Ethical AI: Bias, Fairness and Transparency

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. GDPR: General Data Protection Regulation; HIPAA: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act; FedRAMP: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program; ZDR: zero data retention; BAA: business associate agreement; AI: artificial intelligence; DPA: data processing addendum; PCI: Payment Card Industry; DSS: Data Security Standard; SOC: System and Organization Controls; PII: personally identifiable information; NDA: non-disclosure agreement

  • How to map a regulation to architecture choices (GDPR, HIPAA, FedRAMP)
  • Anthropic's data handling arrangements: retention, ZDR, BAA, residency
  • Which platform routes meet which regime
  • Ethical AI: bias, fairness and transparency in design

2Compliance Is an Architecture Decision

Running case

Lumen Advisory Serves Three Regulated Clients

  • A European retailer (GDPR), a US hospital group (HIPAA) and a federal agency (FedRAMP)
  • Each wants the same assistant; each needs a different platform, contract and data flow

Law is not a certification Claude "has": compliance depends on how and where you process data, the contracts in place and your controls. Always confirm current status with Anthropic and legal counsel [Verify live].

Regime Protects Architecture responses
GDPR (EU personal data) Personal data of people in the EU Lawful basis, minimization, DPA with the processor, data residency or transfer mechanism, retention limits, data-subject rights (access, deletion), records of processing
HIPAA (US health data) Protected health information (PHI) BAA with the vendor, HIPAA-ready configuration and eligible features only, access controls and audit logging, minimum necessary data
FedRAMP (US federal cloud) Federal data in cloud services Use a FedRAMP-authorized route, for example Claude through Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud or Google Cloud Vertex AI with Assured Workloads; the direct Claude API is not FedRAMP authorized [Verify live]
Others (PCI DSS, SOC 2, sector rules) Cards, controls, sector data Tokenize or avoid card data; evidence from the vendor's attestations

3Anthropic Data Handling Arrangements

Arrangement What it means Notes
Standard commercial terms Customer content from the API is not used for training by default; retention is minimal and feature-specific Retained data is never used for training without permission
Zero data retention (ZDR) Anthropic does not store prompts or responses at rest after the response Enabled per organization by the account team; individual features are eligible or not; ZDR organizations cannot call the API from a browser (use a back end)
HIPAA readiness Signed BAA plus a HIPAA-enabled organization; encryption, access control and audit logging Applies to eligible features only; not every feature qualifies (for example some server tools are not HIPAA eligible)
Covered Models Designated models require 30-day retention ZDR is not available for them unless Anthropic authorizes it
Data residency Choose inference geography (inference_geo, for example global or US) Track by usage reports
Cloud platforms On Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud (Google managed) the cloud provider is the data processor; their BAA, DPA, residency and certifications apply Feature availability differs by platform

Design practices for any regime

  • Classify data; send the minimum to the model; mask or tokenize PII before the prompt and restore it after (also possible inside a sandbox).
  • Keep logs free of regulated content or protect and expire them.
  • Enforce access control per user (Module 8); encrypt in transit and at rest.
  • Document data flows, subprocessors, retention and deletion paths.
  • Plan incident response and audit evidence.
  • Check feature eligibility (ZDR or HIPAA) before using a feature in a regulated workflow.
Exam tip

Match the regime to the route and contract: HIPAA = BAA plus HIPAA-ready eligible features; FedRAMP = a FedRAMP-authorized cloud route, not the direct API; GDPR = DPA, minimization and residency. "Any API call is compliant" is the distractor.

4Ethical AI: Bias, Fairness and Transparency

Principle Design practice
Bias Test outputs across demographic and language groups; include diverse cases in evals; review prompts and data for skew; measure disparity (error rate gaps)
Fairness Define the fairness criterion with stakeholders (equal error rates, equal opportunity); keep humans decisive for consequential decisions; provide appeal paths
Transparency Disclose AI involvement; show citations and sources; explain limits and confidence; document the system (what it does and does not do)
Accountability Name an owner; keep audit trails; qualified human review for high-risk uses
Privacy Minimization, consent, retention limits
Safety and non-harm Guardrails, red-teaming, incident response
Provenance Claude outputs can carry watermarks and content credentials: a mark is a signal, not proof; absence proves nothing
  • Fairness is measured, not assumed: add subgroup metrics to the eval suite.
  • High-risk decisions about people need a qualified human who can change the result, and disclosure to the affected person.
  • Be honest about limitations to users and stakeholders (Module 15).
Exam tip

Match the regime to the route and contract: BAA and eligible features, FedRAMP-authorized route, DPA with residency.

Exam tip

Fairness is measured: add subgroup metrics to the eval suite and keep a human decisive for consequential decisions.

5Exam Q&A

S1A US hospital group wants an assistant that processes patient notes through the Claude API. What is required?

  • AA signed BAA with a HIPAA-enabled organization, and use of only HIPAA-eligible features
  • BA browser-based call from the clinician's device to avoid server logs and keep patient data off the back end
  • CZero data retention alone, with no contract changes
  • DNothing beyond an API key, because the API is secure by default and health data is handled the same way
Show the answer

Answer: A. HIPAA needs a BAA and eligible features; other options do not satisfy it.

S2A federal agency needs FedRAMP High for a Claude-based service. Which route fits?

  • AA consumer chat account used by staff
  • BA self-built wrapper around the public website
  • CClaude through a FedRAMP-authorized cloud route such as Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud or Vertex AI with Assured Workloads
  • DThe direct Claude API with an enterprise key
Show the answer

Answer: C. The direct API is not FedRAMP authorized; use an authorized cloud route.

S3A European retailer must limit personal data in prompts and prove processing terms. Which TWO actions help? Select TWO.

  • AMinimize and mask personal data before it reaches the model
  • BSend full customer records to the model for convenience
  • CStore prompts indefinitely so that deletion is unnecessary
  • DPut a data processing addendum and residency settings in place
  • EDisable all logging and documentation
Show the answer

Answer: A, D. Minimization and a DPA with residency address GDPR obligations.

S4A team enables a server tool in a HIPAA workflow without checking eligibility. What is the risk?

  • AThe model will refuse all medical text
  • BThe feature may not be HIPAA eligible, which could break the compliance arrangement
  • CThe feature will double the context window and therefore also double the cost of every HIPAA request
  • DNothing; all features are equal
Show the answer

Answer: B. Check feature eligibility before using it in regulated flows.

S5What does a zero data retention arrangement mean for browser-based calls?

  • AOrganizations with ZDR cannot call the API directly from a browser; use a back end
  • BBrowser calls become mandatory
  • CBrowser calls need no authentication
  • DBrowser calls are cached for thirty days so that repeated requests do not need to be sent again
Show the answer

Answer: A. Cross-origin browser requests are rejected for ZDR organizations.

S6A hiring-support assistant shows a higher error rate for resumes in one language. What should the architect do?

  • AIgnore it, because overall accuracy is high and the subgroup differences are probably just random noise
  • BAdd subgroup evaluation, investigate causes, adjust data or prompts, and keep a human decision-maker
  • CTell users to avoid that language
  • DRemove the language from the evaluation set so that the reported error rates look the same for all groups
Show the answer

Answer: B. Fairness requires measuring disparities and acting on them.

S7Which statement about AI-generated-content marks (watermarks, content credentials) is correct?

  • AA mark proves the content is factually correct and checked, so it can be published without further review
  • BMarks can never be removed or altered
  • CA missing mark proves content is human-made
  • DA detected mark is a signal, not proof, and a missing mark does not prove content is human-made
Show the answer

Answer: D. A detected mark is a useful signal rather than proof, and a missing mark proves nothing about who wrote the content.

S8Models designated as Covered Models require what retention?

  • AIndefinite retention
  • BNo retention rules apply to these models, so each customer decides whether to store anything at all
  • C30-day retention, so ZDR is not available for them unless authorized
  • DZero retention only
Show the answer

Answer: C. Covered Models require 30-day retention, so zero data retention is not available for them unless Anthropic authorizes it.

S9A consultant says "Claude is HIPAA compliant" and proposes using any API feature. Which response is right?

  • AAgree if the client signs an NDA
  • BAgree, since Anthropic holds every possible attestation
  • CDisagree, because Claude can never process health data
  • DCompliance depends on the BAA, configuration, eligible features and your controls, not on a blanket claim
Show the answer

Answer: D. Regimes are met by contract, configuration and controls.

S10Which practice best supports transparency to end users?

  • AProviding answers without sources to keep them short and avoid exposing the retrieval system to readers
  • BHiding that a model is used to avoid confusion
  • CDescribing the system as always correct
  • DDisclosing AI involvement, showing citations and explaining limits
Show the answer

Answer: D. Transparency means disclosing AI involvement, showing citations and sources, and being honest about the system's limits.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
GDPR Lawful basis, minimization, DPA, residency, retention, rights
HIPAA BAA, HIPAA-ready org, eligible features only, audit logging
FedRAMP Authorized route: Bedrock in GovCloud or Vertex with Assured Workloads; direct API not authorized
ZDR No storage at rest; per org; feature eligibility; no browser calls
Covered Models 30-day retention; no ZDR
Cloud platforms Provider is the processor; its contracts apply
Practice Classify, minimize, mask, access control, document, incident plan
Ethics Subgroup testing, human decisions, disclosure, citations, accountability
Marks Signal not proof
